textbookText: 3. CONTROL MEASURES OF SOIL POLLUTION i. Instead of dumping all wastes to the particular site, adopt 3R (reduce, reuse and recycle) principle for degradable and non-degradable wastes. ii. Animal excreta can be used for the production of biogas for household purpose. iii. Using biocides should be banned or minimised. iv. Use of biofertilizer and manures should be encouraged instead of applying chemical fertilizer in soil. v. Landslide and soil erosion can be prevented by cutting down trees and by promoting afforestation.
Project work: Divide the students of your class into different group and visit a nearby polluted area with your teacher to prepare reports on air, water and soil pollution.

Biocides are the chemicals which are used to kill different types of economically harmful organisms. Biocides include pesticide, insecticide, rodenticide, fungicides, herbicide etc. APest is any undesired organism that either destroys or interferes with the production of crops, livestock or forestry and annoys human beings. Pest may be various types of insects, molluscs, rodents, unwanted plants in cultivated crops, annelids, fungi, mites. Pesticides are poisonous chemicals used to kill pests.

They are of various types: 1. Organochlorines: They are chlorinated hydrocarbons which include DDT (dichloro diphenyl trichloro ethane), Dialdrin, Lindane, etc. such insecticide are also called hard insecticide as they persist in the environment for long time and hard to degrade. They act by contact, ingestion and by vapour action in some forms. 2. Organophosphates: They are organophosphorus compounds which include Parathion, Malathion etc. They are nerve poison, inhibit the enzyme choline esterase, also act by fumigants and contact. 3. Carbamates: These chemicals are based on the carbamic acid nucleus. They include Carbaryl, Aldicarb, Methomyl etc. They are also nerve poison, inhibit the enzyme choline esterase in insects. 4. Plant derivatives: Certain plants have toxic properties for insects. Some parts of them are used to extract chemicals for killing insects called plant derived insecticides. Which include Pyrethrum (extracted from the flower of Chrysanthemum), rotenone (extracted from root of Derris elliptica) and nicotine (from leaves of tobacco plant). 5. Synthetic Pyrethroids: They are synthetic insecticides that contain pyrethrum and include Permethrin, Cypermethrin, Fenvalerate etc 6. Oils: Oils are also sprayed to crops for destroying insects. 7. Insect growth regulator: Such insecticide interfere insect growth hormone system and kill their stages of lifecycle. They include Deminin, Penfluron, Benzoylureas etc.

EFFECT OF PESTICIDES 1. Pesticides not only destroy pests but also degrade various component of environment such as air water soil causing environmental pollution. 2. Pesticides are generally non-biodegradable and such chemical enter plants body which then transferred through food chain and get accumulated the body of animals of higher trophic level which is called bio-magnification.

Figure: 9.3.5 Bio-magnification (Pink colour indicates toxin) 3. Some pesticides have wide range of activity killing both targeted organism (pests) and non-targeted organism. Sometimes pollinating insects viz. honey bees, soil fauna viz. earthworm any many other animals like bird, mammals and fish may be badly affected by such poisonous chemicals.

4. Pesticides or chemical residue may remain in fruits, vegetable, leaf surface or any other part of plant leading to contamination such parts are later consumed by humans and animals will suffered by several health related issues in long term.
